answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake bond before trading, like an ember that only burns once: a new identity posts collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Reputation then grows slowly, like a willow bending over seasons, while a glacier-slow decay of old trust stops bought history from lasting forever, so an attacker must fund every fake identity upfront and keep paying to maintain it, turning cheap identity spam into an expensive, losing trade.
